claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I have one child I'd like to check about - my son Alex. He's 12 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I'm just wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Before I can determine your eligibility, I need to gather a bit more detail about your situation and Alex.

Let me start by reading the eligibility rules to ensure I ask you the right questions.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I have the eligibility rules. Based on what you've told me, Alex is 12 years old and lives with you in the UK. Let me ask my first question to check his eligibility:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education, training, or does he attend school as normal?** (This helps me confirm he meets the basic requirements, as the rules apply to children under 16 in education or those under 20 in approved education/training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he goes to school like any normal 12-year-old. He's in Year 8 at our local secondary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful - Alex is in normal full-time education, which is good.

Now I need to check a few more details about your circumstances:

**Are you currently living in the UK, and is Alex living with you full-time (not living with someone else)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. I live in the UK and Alex lives here at home with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. That's clear - Alex lives with you full-time in the UK.

Now I have one more important question:

**Are you, or is anyone else, currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody is claiming Child Benefit for him at the moment. That's why I'm asking about it now - I wanted to see if I could claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, that's very helpful to know. Let me ask just one more question to complete my assessment:

**What is your immigration status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or do you have another form of right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, born and raised here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the eligibility rules and your circumstances, let me provide my outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's a summary of why:
- Alex is 12 years old (under 16, so eligible)
- He lives with you full-time in the UK
- You are responsible for him and a British citizen
- He is in full-time education at secondary school
- No one else is claiming for him

You can now go ahead and make a claim for Child Benefit. If you have any other questions or if your circumstances change, feel free to reach out or contact HMRC directly.
